messages:
alex_infra: Anyone else seeing a spike in RPC errors to model-service around 10:12 UTC? Lots of 5xx and timeouts, traces point to DNS lookups failing (timeouts) from inference pods.

marta_sre: Yep, I'm getting alerts. node-local-dns on several GPU nodes shows repeated SERVFAIL and upstream timeouts in the logs.

kevin_gpu: Also seeing pods getting delayed at startup because the scheduler blocks on service DNS resolution — some inference jobs timed out and retried. GPU nodes have elevated node-cache CPU.

sara_sys: Pulled the node-local-dns logs from one affected host: ```kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/node-local-dns -c node-cache --tail=60```
2026-03-18T10:12:13Z [WARN] cache miss for model-service.default.svc.cluster.local
2026-03-18T10:12:13Z [ERR] upstream query timeout for model-service.default.svc.cluster.local -> 8.8.8.8
2026-03-18T10:12:14Z [WARN] query backlog exceeded, dropping new queries

alex_infra: I ran tcpdump on the host NIC and I'm seeing lots of fragmented UDP and intermittent ICMP "fragmentation needed" / "packet too big". When payloads > 1500 bytes we lose packets, smaller ones mostly fine. Suspect MTU mismatch on calico/vxlan or RDMA offload interacting badly.

marta_sre: On eu-west-1a infra team reported an interface flap earlier this morning. I ran a quick perf test between two GPU nodes: 8kB UDP packets show ~0.6% loss, 64B packets show ~0.01% loss.

kevin_gpu: This smells like UDP GSO/GRO + RDMA NIC offload + jumbo frames. Kernel may try to offload segmentation and the calico vxlan decapsulator ends up dropping or misordering fragments. Node-local-dns uses lots of small/medium UDP queries and times out when upstream answer never arrives.

sara_sys: Quick mitigation proposal: increase node-local-dns cache size/TTL, reduce upstream timeouts, and add a fallback upstream (regional coredns) so the pod-level cache doesn't immediately hit upstream for every miss. I'm prepping a small k8s patch.

marta_sre: Also consider increasing conntrack and ephemeral port ranges — clients are opening many short UDP sockets for DNS and we borderline hit ephemeral port exhaustion on a few hosts. Could exacerbate retries.

alex_infra: @kevin_gpu can you try disabling offloads on one affected host to validate? Command: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 rx off tx off gso off gro off tso off` — do it on a single node and monitor DNS success rate.

kevin_gpu: Running it now on gpu-node-17. Will report in 2m.

dns-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 - DNS node-cache timeouts impacting inference. Severity: P2. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0423

kevin_gpu: After disabling offloads on gpu-node-17 DNS timeout rate dropped ~90% for pods on that node. Services recovered, RPC errors cleared for those replicas. Looks like offload + MTU mismatch is the culprit.

sara_sys: Good reproducer. Rolling the disable to the other 4 problematic GPU hosts in the same AZ for now. Will also patch node-local-dns to add a secondary upstream and bump cache TTL to 30s to reduce upstream pressure.

marta_sre: Long-term options to evaluate: 1) normalize MTU across RDMA and overlay networks, 2) disable problematic offloads in our GPU AMI or tune driver settings, 3) switch critical DNS to TCP for reliability, 4) consider hostNetwork node-local-dns for GPU fleet, 5) autoscale CoreDNS and add circuit-breakers.

alex_infra: Also callout on cost: retries and delayed start caused the cluster-autoscaler to spin up extra inference replicas, adding ~\$2k of GPU spend during the incident window. We should add an alert that ties DNS error rate to autoscaler events.

kevin_gpu: I'll draft an RFC for driver/kernel changes and a test plan for MTU/offload combos. For now the rolling disable + node-local-dns patch should buy time.

sara_sys: I'll update the incident ticket with mitigation steps and a short runbook for on-call. Postmortem to follow once we have kernel logs and NIC vendor analysis. Thanks everyone.

marta_sre: :thumbsup: tagging infra/networking to follow up on AZ link flaps and confirm hardware health.

alex_infra: Closing thread once the incident page is updated and rolling changes complete.
